Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Depressive symptoms (BDI-II) were lower in vitamin D-treated women than in untreated women with Hashimoto's thyroiditis.
Sentence: "The BDI-II score was lowest in the vitamin D-treated women and highest in the untreated patients with thyroiditis."
Measured as: depressive symptoms (BDI-II)
Population: Young euthyroid women with Hashimoto's thyroiditis, untreated or receiving vitamin D, selenomethionine or myo-inositol
Intervention: Vitamin D (dose and duration not reported)
Comparator: Untreated women, and women receiving selenomethionine or myo-inositol
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: not reported
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: In the univariate analysis, vitamin D levels showed no significant association with depression or other geriatric assessment variables, apart from hypertension.
Sentence: "In univariate analysis, no significant associations were found between vitamin D and other variables, except for hypertension (p = 0.049)."
Measured as: depression (geriatric assessment)
Population: Elderly individuals aged 65-100 years receiving home healthcare services
Intervention: Serum vitamin D level (measured, not administered)
Comparator: Vitamin D categories (severe deficiency, deficiency, other groups)
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 439
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported
